about: workflow:keep-community-events-and-rsvps: keeps a space's events and each person's RSVP in the space's own store, in one batch per operation with a revision check, so a stale write is refused and a full event refuses a new going. It replaces the records-door adapter of tools/run-a-community (read-data/community-memberships.mjs, which read and wrote the membership and member records through the door, with its own transactions and compare-and-swap) and the store calls of read-data/community-events.mjs. The rules that decide the rows are tools/run-a-community/read-data/community-event-records.mjs (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep community events and RSVPs
payload.job: Keep a space's events (one or a repeating series, moved, or cancelled with their RSVPs) and each person's RSVP, in the space's own store: a write is whole or not at all and only on the revision it was read at, a full event refuses a new going, a leaving RSVP is kept as left, and a read gives a person the events that overlap a range, in order.
payload.produces: The store's own event and RSVP objects, proven on the example operations and probes in two kinds of store, and each run's events and RSVPs kept, refused and read back.

source.from: the owner, 2026-11-18, and the W3.2b lane brief: run-a-community keeps events as the space's membership rows and RSVPs as their member rows; a tool keeps no record, the store does
source.note: Ported from the retired Worker's community event actions (source commit b6ae0ebf815f2f5271eed34e6e023c7e1767ec04; see tools/run-a-community/source-baselines). Who may act (membership, invitation and paid access) stays in the tool as values, and so do the repeat times and the calendar invitation. The rows and their batches stay with the store. The planning rules are tools/run-a-community/read-data/community-event-records.mjs.

where.description: Where the space's events are kept: the store's own address, as the person's store row names it

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses for that store, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the events are kept, when the person has a place for them already

community.description: The space: {id, title, events} where events is members or everyone (its configuration row)

operations.description: Each operation: create (event_ids, times, relay, title, size_limit, series_id, now), rsvp (event, relay, going, now), move (event, relay, input), cancel (event, relay), read (from, to, relay, member, sees_meetings, may_put_on)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit kept_in (where the space's events and RSVPs are kept, or null) and objects (the names of the objects that already answer each question below).

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found no such objects, make them in the store's own form: (1) one table of space rows, each event a row with its title, words, start, end, size limit, creator, series and revision; (2) one table of RSVP rows keyed by event and person, each with its state (member or left), role, changed time and revision; (3) a rule that a row is written only if its revision is the one it was read at, or it is new, and that a batch of rows is written whole or not at all; (4) a rule that an RSVP row leaves the store only with its event (in the same batch); (5) a read of a space's events that overlap a range, in start order. Grant only what the store needs for these.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example operations
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, run these operations in order, each through the store's own objects, the planning rules computing which rows each batch writes and with which revision: [{"id": "o1", "op": "create", "relay": "owner", "event_ids": ["e1"], "title": "Club", "size_limit": 2, "series_id": null, "times": [{"starts_at": "2026-11-20T10:00:00.000Z", "ends_at": "2026-11-20T11:00:00.000Z"}], "now": "2026-11-18T09:00:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o2", "op": "create", "relay": "owner", "event_ids": ["e2a", "e2b"], "title": "Weekly", "size_limit": null, "series_id": "s1", "times": [{"starts_at": "2026-11-21T18:00:00.000Z", "ends_at": "2026-11-21T19:00:00.000Z"}, {"starts_at": "2026-11-28T18:00:00.000Z", "ends_at": "2026-11-28T19:00:00.000Z"}], "now": "2026-11-18T09:01:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o3", "op": "rsvp", "event": "e1", "relay": "m1", "going": true, "now": "2026-11-18T09:02:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o4", "op": "rsvp", "event": "e1", "relay": "m2", "going": true, "now": "2026-11-18T09:03:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o5", "op": "rsvp", "event": "e1", "relay": "m3", "going": true, "now": "2026-11-18T09:04:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o6", "op": "rsvp", "event": "e1", "relay": "m1", "going": false, "now": "2026-11-18T09:05:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o7", "op": "rsvp", "event": "e1", "relay": "m3", "going": true, "now": "2026-11-18T09:06:00.000Z"}, {"id": "o8", "op": "move", "event": "e1", "relay": "m3", "input": {"starts_at": "2026-11-20T11:00:00.000Z", "title": "Club evening"}}, {"id": "o9", "op": "cancel", "event": "e2b", "relay": "owner"}, {"id": "o10", "op": "read", "from": "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z", "to": "2026-12-01T00:00:00.000Z", "relay": "m3", "member": true, "sees_meetings": true, "may_put_on": false}] Then try each probe ([{"id": "p1", "op": "stale-move", "event": "e1", "expected_revision": 1}, {"id": "p2", "op": "insert-existing", "event": "e1"}, {"id": "p3", "op": "remove-member-alone", "member": "e1:m2"}]). Submit results, refusals (each operation refused and the store's words), rows (every row read back), space (the read of the community's events), and probes (refused or changed).

checks.says: Every example operation is kept or refused as the intent says, every probe is refused, and the store's own objects give every expected answer

steps.title: Keep this run's operations
steps.do: For each operation: read the space's events and RSVPs the operation touches; plan its rows with the rules (a new event or series, a move keeping the length, a cancellation with its RSVPs, an RSVP with the full-event rule, or the space read); write the batch whole, each row with the revision it was read at; refuse and say why when the rules or the store refuse. Submit results, refused, kept_ids (the rows written) and found_ids (every row read back).

checks.says: Every row written is read back
